title: Your First Memory Might Never Have Happened
request: Biku's What's the Catch? Short, used as it is: 'create short based on this and remember since the time has been reduced to 1 min the drawing and animation must be good' (2026-10-23). The first Short in the toned look (2), the calm camera, gauges and the Kurzgesagt Short rules.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Think of your very first memory. Got it?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There's a good chance it never *happened*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some people even say they remember being *born*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Clue one: most people's oldest real memory is from around age *three*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before that, the brain keeps almost nothing, a blank scientists call *childhood amnesia*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Clue two: a British survey asked over six thousand people for their first *memory*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nearly four in ten said it came from age two or *younger*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And almost nine hundred said one or younger.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Clue three: a lot of those baby memories are about a *pram*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But look: this one is seen from *above*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A baby in a pram could never see that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So here's the catch: the feeling may be real, but the *picture* came later.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Researchers think it was stitched together from family *photos* and stories told at dinner.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So is your first memory real? If it's from before age three, probably *not*.

sources: Akhtar, S., Justice, L. V., Morrison, C. M. and Conway, M. A., "Fictional First Memories", Psychological Science, 2018, 29(10): 1612-1619. A survey of 6,641 people in the UK: average age of first memory 3.2 years; 2,487 (nearly 40%) dated it to age two or younger and 893 to age one or younger; the authors judge these likely fictional. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797618778831

City, University of London, "Forty per cent of people have a fictional first memory, says study", 2018. Fragments of early experience combined with facts from photographs or family talk; a typical example is a memory of a pram; the person does not know it is fictional. https://www.citystgeorges.ac.uk/news-and-events/news/2018/07/forty-per-cent-of-people-have-a-fictional-first-memory-says-study
